name: Aplestosuchus
sum: Aplestosuchus is an extinct baurusuchid crocodyliform from the Late Cretaceous Adamantina Formation of Brazil, known from a skeleton with the remains of its last prey.
wsnote: No body-length estimate is given in the sources consulted.
holotype: LPRP/USP 0229a, an articulated, nearly complete skeleton including the skull (Buruti creek area, General Salgado, São Paulo; Adamantina Formation).
material: The holotype only; teeth and skull bones of an unidentified sphagesaurid crocodyliform (LPRP/USP 0229b) lay in its abdominal cavity.
exceptional: Stomach contents - remains of a sphagesaurid crocodyliform, direct evidence of predation between crocodyliform taxa.
biology: The sphagesaurid remains in the abdominal cavity are direct evidence that it preyed on other crocodyliforms.
author: Godoy et al. 2014
